chunks: Muhammad ibn 'Ali ibn Mahbub, from Ahmad ibn al-Hasan ibn 'Ali, from 'Amr ibn Sa'id, from Musaddiq ibn Sadaqah, from 'Ammar al-Sabati, who said:
I asked Aba 'Abdillah عليه السلام about a man who performed wudu (ablution) and then ate meat or fish: may he perform salat (prayer) without washing his hand?

He said: "Yes. But if it was milk, he should not perform salat (prayer) until he washes his hand and rinses his mouth. The Messenger of Allah صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم would perform salat (prayer) after eating meat without washing his hand; but if it was milk, he would not perform salat (prayer) until he washed his hand and rinsed his mouth."

key_terms.لَبَنٌ: milk, which has a distinct ruling here
key_terms.يَغْسِلَ يَدَهُ: to wash his hand before prayer

ai.seo_question: Can a person pray after eating meat, fish, or milk without washing their hand?
ai.summary: This hadith gives a legal ruling concerning prayer after eating, distinguishing between meat or fish and milk. It indicates that eating meat or fish does not require washing the hand before salat (prayer), while milk entails washing the hand and rinsing the mouth, and it cites the practice of the Messenger of Allah صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم as precedent.
